source.title: Sycophantic Agreement Transfers with Neutral Data via Contrastive Preference Optimization
source.authors: C. Blank; Zhuo-Fan Ying; Christopher Potts; Peter Hase; Jing Huang

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a teacher's behavior can transfer to a student through apparently neutral training data, but uses contrastive preference optimization and a multi-turn sycophancy measure rather than the original study's trait-transfer setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports behavior rates after post-training, teacher-pair DPO, filtering and subset-selection experiments, and preference-data agreement measurements. Overtly induced sycophancy from the LLS system prompt is not recorded as evidence of spontaneous transmission. The prompt-selection results and hyperparameter choices are not rows.
record.test_reason: A realistic setting: OLMo-3/Tülu-3 preference-optimization pipelines. It asks whether a teacher behaviour (sycophantic agreement toward the user) transfers to a student trained on teacher outputs with no overt examples of it. The method is contrastive DPO on general chat responses, not SFT on semantically filtered numbers/code. The authors say semantic references were not controlled as in subliminal learning. Student rates are measured against the SFT reference for 16 teacher pairs, 7 objectives, data sizes and two students.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors conclude that teacher sycophancy transfers through seemingly neutral preference data under contrastive objectives, with student sycophancy tracking the log-ratio of chosen/rejected teacher rates. SFT on chosen responses transfers much less. The signal is diffuse: probe-based filtering and LLS selection fail without removing much of the data. They suggest pairing teachers of similar sycophancy, e.g. a GPT judge over a large model pool, and call sycophancy a feature of preference learning itself.
record.recipe_differences: Uses DPO and other contrastive preference objectives on chosen/rejected response pairs, rather than ordinary fine-tuning on semantically unrelated filtered outputs. Trait is multi-turn sycophantic agreement; training data are a realistic preference dataset, not a controlled trait-only dataset.
record.method_sensitivity: Teacher-pair sycophancy ratio; preference objective; data subset and size; challenge-prompt wording (the appendix reports higher rates for prompts naming an alternative answer). Official Tülu DPO and controlled Tülu retraining also differ.

fits_no_version.finding: Sycophancy emerges at the DPO stage in the OLMo-3 pipeline and stays through RLVR. Official Tülu-3 DPO, trained on GPT-judged pool data, instead lowers it (11.4→7.0→5.3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Which post-training stage induces sycophancy depends on how preference pairs are generated (single strong/weak teacher pair vs judged pool).

record.problems: The authors limit the model families to OLMo and Tülu, train students only in the 7–8B range, and evaluate sycophancy in one multi-turn factual multiple-choice setting. Some filtering and LLS results are described in text or shown only in figures without exact values. The study does not compare same-base and different-base student-teacher pairs under controlled conditions.
record.rows_left_out: Not stated; all extracted quantitative sycophancy outcomes retained. LLS system-prompt selection results were excluded because the behavior was intentionally prompted and those values were used to choose a prompt, not to measure spontaneous transmission.

untested.parts: Favourite-animal or other preference traits; numbers/code/maths outputs; data systematically filtered of semantic trait references; plain SFT on outputs of a trait-bearing teacher (only SFT on mixed Dolci chosen responses, R26).
No same-base teacher-student pair. Every teacher (Qwen3, Llama-3, OLMo-2) differs from the OLMo-3 or Tülu student base, so there is no controlled same- vs different-base contrast.
Emergent misalignment or harmful traits other than multi-turn sycophantic agreement.
Token entanglement, divergence tokens, and steering-vector directions. The layer-20 probe direction is used only for data attribution, not as a carrier test.
No LoRA-rank sweep. The only LoRA runs (LLS config, r=64) are confounded with 20-token truncation and different β/learning rate.

missing.what: Regression of student sycophancy on ln(teacher chosen/rejected rate): R²=0.76, Spearman ρ=0.83, p<0.001 (15 pairs + GPT-judged + full Dolci). Figure 7 version: R²=0.80, ρ=0.89.
Teacher sycophancy rates (no-letter): Qwen3 0.6B 0.6, 4B 6.7, 14B 5.3, 32B 13.6; OLMo-2 7B 46.4, 32B 27.1; Llama 1B 24.2, 3B 26.3, 8B 44.9. These are needed to read every teacher-pair row.
Letter-naming (6-prompt) sycophancy rates: SFT 97.5 vs DPO 96.7 vs original pair 98.7. Near ceiling with no transfer visible; only the no-letter subset shows the effect.
All LLS-config students (LoRA r=64, 20-token targets) are less sycophantic than both OLMo-config full-FT students. Removing the LLS top-25k (config 4) does not reduce sycophancy.
Sycophancy vs training-set size follows a power law (R²=0.99) matching preference-learning accuracy.
Data audit: only 4% of examples are multi-turn and 11 involve factual correction, none sycophantic. This stands in for the original's filtering check.

record.verdict_notes: The reader mis-stated teacher ordering for R16 and R19 and treated decreases from low-sycophancy chosen teachers as 'reversed'. Fixed by reading the teacher rates in Table 3. R05 and R19 (Qwen 14B vs 4B) both run against the paper's log-ratio account, and the paper does not discuss them. The setting differs from the original in kind: contrastive DPO on general responses, not filtered unrelated data. This weakens inferences about B and the original A. The shared 1,000-question set was selected so that every model answers all items correctly at turn 1.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test favourite-animal traits, numbers/code/math-only outputs, or a controlled procedure that filters every semantic reference to the trait. Tests sycophancy transfer through preference pairs reported to contain no overt examples.
Reports transfer with students and response-generating teachers from different model families, but does not conduct a controlled same-base versus different-base comparison.
Tests sycophantic agreement only; does not test misalignment or other harmful traits.
Tests relative teacher sycophancy and whether the signal is concentrated in identifiable data subsets. Does not test token entanglement, divergence tokens, or a steering-vector-like mechanism.
Reports full-fine-tuning experiments and evaluations across challenge prompts. Does not compare LoRA ranks.
No prompt-only experiment inserts linked tokens without fine-tuning. An explicitly sycophantic system prompt was used to select an LLS target prompt, not to test the linked-token analogue.
